title: $τ$-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
research_question: Benchmark agent-user-tool interaction; measure reliability of agent behavior over multiple trials
models: GPT-4o and other function-calling LLMs (closed; no open <=7B)
core_finding: Introduces pass^k; frontier function-calling agents solve <50% of tasks and are highly inconsistent (pass^8<25% in retail).
limitation: Closed frontier models only; no open small models, no precision or fine-tuning axis.

title: ReliabilityBench: Evaluating LLM Agent Reliability Under Production-Like Stress Conditions
research_question: Benchmark agent reliability jointly over repetition, task perturbation and injected tool faults
models: Gemini 2.0 Flash, GPT-4o (both closed)
core_finding: Defines a reliability surface R(k,eps,lambda); perturbations alone cut success from 96.9% to 88.1%, rate limiting is the most damaging fault, and ReAct is more robust than Reflexion under combined stress.
limitation: Two closed models only, no open or small models, no precision or fine-tuning axis.

title: On Randomness in Agentic Evals
research_question: How much does single-run pass@1 misestimate agentic benchmark performance?
models: 3 models x 2 scaffolds (not named in abstract)
core_finding: Single-run pass@1 varies by 2.2-6.0 pp and SD exceeds 1.5 pp even at temperature 0, so reported 2-3 pp gains can be evaluation noise; trajectories diverge within the first few percent of tokens.
limitation: Code-agent domain only; no small open models, no precision axis.

title: When Agents Disagree With Themselves: Behavioral Consistency as an Uncertainty Signal for LLM Agents
pub_status: workshop (ICML 2026 Workshop on Statistical Frameworks for Uncertainty in Agentic Systems)
research_question: Is run-to-run behavioral variance of an agent a usable black-box uncertainty signal?
models: 4 models incl. Llama (open); exact sizes not in abstract
repeated_runs: yes, n=10 per question (8,000 runs); 1,000 runs on SWE-bench
core_finding: Identical inputs yield 2.3-4.2 distinct action sequences per 10 runs; consistent tasks reach 82-87% accuracy vs 41-65% for inconsistent ones, and k=3 agreement gives selective prediction at 87-88% accuracy / 54-62% coverage.
limitation: No precision/quantization axis and no fine-tuning axis; this is exactly the paper candidate A proposes to replicate.

title: Measuring the Unmeasurable: Markov Chain Reliability for LLM Agents
research_question: Can agent reliability be given a fitted statistical model rather than a scalar metric?
models: not specified in abstract
core_finding: Fits agent traces to an absorbing discrete-time Markov chain with AIC/KS goodness-of-fit checks and Dirichlet/bootstrap intervals, arguing pass@k, pass^k and reliability-decay curves do not identify the underlying success-time distribution.
limitation: Methodological; no comparison across model precisions or fine-tuned variants.

title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Measuring Cross-Lingual Policy Retention in Tool-Using Agents
research_question: Does a tool-using agent take the same actions when the same task is posed in another language?
models: 8 models (open and closed; sizes not in abstract)
repeated_runs: yes, 2.38M rollouts incl. same-question repeats as baseline
core_finding: Action-policy divergence across languages is structural rather than sampling noise: it survives greedy decoding in every cell and stays flat as temperature rises, and five confounds (trace length, empty traces, chance agreement, each model's own reproducibility ceiling) each individually flip conclusions if uncorrected.
limitation: Cross-lingual axis, not precision; but supplies the confound controls candidate A would need.

title: Harness Engineering for Predictable Agentic Systems: An Empirical Study of Deterministic Execution Constraints
research_question: Does harness engineering (deterministic execution constraints) improve run-to-run reproducibility of LLM agents?
models: Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct (open-weight, ≤7B), Gemma-3-27B (open-weight, >7B)
benchmarks: Two synthetic tasks: finance and legal agent tasks
core_finding: Structured Planning validation eliminates agent run-to-run variance, reaching Reproducibility Rate/Determinism Index of 1.000 in 3 of 4 model-task cells.
limitation: Does not study quantization or LoRA fine-tuning effects, and uses only one ≤7B open model without HotpotQA-style distractor QA tasks.

title: Tools in the Loop: Quantifying Uncertainty of LLM Question Answering Systems That Use Tools
research_question: How should uncertainty be quantified when an LLM answers using external tools?
models: not enumerated in abstract
core_finding: Extends token-sequence uncertainty quantification to jointly account for LLM and tool-output uncertainty in tool-calling QA systems.
limitation: Single-tool QA rather than multi-step agent loops.

title: How Can Input Reformulation Improve Tool Usage Accuracy in a Complex Dynamic Environment? A Study on $τ$-bench
research_question: Can input reformulation improve tool-use accuracy and consistency on tau-bench?
models: not enumerated in abstract
core_finding: The IRMA reformulation framework beats ReAct, function calling and self-reflection by 16.1%, 12.7% and 19.1% in overall pass^5.
limitation: Uses pass^5 as an outcome metric but does not analyse the variance structure itself.

title: MAESTRO: Multi-Agent Evaluation Suite for Testing, Reliability, and Observability
research_question: How reliable/reproducible are multi-agent system executions across repeated runs, backends, tool configs?
models: Unspecified backend models tested; no confirmation of open-weight ≤7B models used
benchmarks: 12 representative MAS across agentic frameworks/interaction patterns
core_finding: MAS executions are structurally stable but temporally variable, with architecture dominating resource/reproducibility trade-offs over backend model changes.
limitation: Focuses on multi-agent systems broadly rather than small open-weight agents, quantization, or LoRA fine-tuning specifically.

title: Confident and Wrong: Silent Semantic Failures in Coding Agents
research_question: Do coding agents consistently produce wrong-but-plausible patches across repeated runs, undermining trust metrics?
models: GPT-5, Llama 4, Gemini, and one other frontier model; no open-weight model ≤7B
core_finding: Submit rate and resolve rate diverge sharply, with 'silent semantic failure' (consistent plausible-but-wrong patches) dominating failures across repeated runs.
limitation: Uses only large frontier/Llama 4 models on SWE-bench coding tasks, not small open-weight agents or HotpotQA, and does not study quantization or LoRA.

title: InconLens: Interactive Visual Diagnosis of Behavioral Inconsistencies in LLM-based Agentic Systems
research_question: How to visually diagnose behavioral inconsistencies across repeated runs of LLM agents on same input?
models: Not specified in abstract; no explicit small open-weight model named
benchmarks: Not specified; case study on agentic tasks
core_finding: InconLens visual analytics tool helps developers identify divergence points and failure modes across repeated agent runs.
limitation: Proposes a diagnostic/visualization tool rather than systematic quantitative variance metrics or comparison across quantization/fine-tuning settings.

title: Beyond pass@1: A Reliability Science Framework for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
research_question: How does reliability/consistency of LLM agents diverge from capability across repeated attempts and task duration?
models: 10 unnamed models evaluated; sizes/openness not specified in abstract
core_finding: Reliability and capability diverge systematically with task duration, with domain-stratified decay and rank inversions.
limitation: No quantization or LoRA fine-tuning analysis, and no confirmed small open-weight agent, limiting direct relevance beyond the consistency-metric methodology.

title: Claw-Eval: Towards Trustworthy Evaluation of Autonomous Agents
research_question: Can trajectory-aware grading make autonomous-agent evaluation trustworthy?
models: 14 frontier models
core_finding: Trajectory-opaque grading misses 44% of safety violations, and reporting Pass^k over three trials separates genuine capability from lucky single runs.
limitation: Only 3 trials; frontier models only.

title: ROZA Graphs: Self-Improving Near-Deterministic RAG through Evidence-Centric Feedback
research_question: Does persisting evidence-centric reasoning graphs improve accuracy and run-to-run decision consistency in RAG agents?
models: Claude Sonnet 4, Haiku 4.5, GPT-5-mini; no open-weight model, none ≤7B
core_finding: Reasoning/retrieval graph context engineering raises accuracy and per-passage decision consistency across repeated runs without modifying model weights.
limitation: Uses only large proprietary/closed models, no quantization or LoRA fine-tuning, so irrelevant to small open-weight agent consistency under compression/tuning.

title: Don't Overthink It: Inter-Rollout Action Agreement as a Free Adaptive-Compute Signal for LLM Agents
research_question: Can inter-rollout action agreement be used to allocate inference compute per step?
models: not fully specified in abstract
repeated_runs: yes, small candidate sets per step
core_finding: A training-free controller that samples candidate actions per step and commits when agreement is high matches or beats fixed-budget self-consistency at lower cost.
limitation: Very small task counts (50 and 30); uses agreement as a control signal rather than measuring consistency itself.

title: Computer Use at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
research_question: Are computer-use agent benchmarks and pass@k aggregation methodologically sound?
models: frontier models (not enumerated in abstract)
core_finding: A blind replay script that never observes the screen beats frontier models on static benchmarks, and its expected success rate provably equals the source agent's pass@k in deterministic environments, indicting naive pass@k aggregation for stateful tasks.
limitation: GUI/computer-use domain; the critique transfers but the setting does not.

title: More Is Not Always Better: Cross-Component Interference in LLM Agent Scaffolding
research_question: Do stacked agent scaffolding components interfere destructively?
models: Llama-3.1-8B and 70B (open; 8B near the project's range)
repeated_runs: yes, up to 10 seeds per condition (96 conditions)
core_finding: A full 2^5 factorial over five scaffolding components shows the all-components agent is consistently suboptimal (single-tool agent beats it by 32% F1 on HotpotQA, p=0.023) and 56.3% of subsets violate submodularity.
limitation: Measures mean performance across seeds, not run-to-run consistency as an outcome in its own right.

title: $τ$-Rec: A Verifiable Benchmark for Agentic Recommender Systems
research_question: Can agentic recommender evaluation use verifiable rewards plus a reliability metric?
models: GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Qwen3-32B, GPT-5 mini
core_finding: A steep reliability cliff: the best configuration reaches ~57% pass^1 but only ~35% pass^4.
limitation: Recommender domain; smallest open model is 32B, above the project's hardware range.

title: Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0: Can LLMs Find the Same Bugs Twice?
research_question: How repeatable are agentic LLM vulnerability-finding results across repeated runs on same JS code?
models: Claude (agentic LLM); no open-weight model, no model ≤7B used
benchmarks: Snyk VulnBench JS; JavaScript vulnerability-finding benchmark vs Snyk Code SAST
core_finding: Reference-matched LLM findings were highly stable across 5 repetitions, but unmatched extra findings varied heavily run to run.
limitation: Uses only a large closed-weight model (Claude) on security review, not small open-weight agents or quantization/fine-tuning effects.

title: The Remarkable Effectiveness of Providing AI Agents with Natural Language Tools: A Replication Study Validating NLT Performance Across 14 Models
research_question: Does replacing structured tool calling with natural-language tools improve agent reliability?
models: 14 models incl. open-weight and smaller models
core_finding: Natural-language tools raise tool-calling accuracy by 14.9 pp and cut critical errors by 93%, with the largest gains (+24.0 to +43.1 pp) for smaller models and models lacking native tool calling.
limitation: Replication of a specific framework; shows harness design is a large confound for small-model agent reliability.

title: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
research_question: Does giving a computer-use agent text tools help or hurt, and why?
models: one reasoning and one non-reasoning model
repeated_runs: yes, n=5 per condition (effects reported vs 2 SE)
core_finding: The same MCP tools improve a reasoning model by +4.0 pp and degrade a non-reasoning model by -5.9 pp under one identical harness, and RL makes tool-use behavior steerable without making competence follow.
limitation: Only 5 runs per cell; GUI domain.

title: SkillSentry: Reliable Skill Execution for LLM Agents via Runtime Assurance
research_question: Can runtime assurance improve reliability/consistency of LLM agent skill execution across repeated runs?
models: Claude Code (Claude-Haiku-4.5, Claude-Opus-4.6), Codex (GPT-5.2, GPT-5.4); no small open-weight model used
benchmarks: 15 custom skills across two agent frameworks
core_finding: SkillSentry improves task success rate by 24.1% on average while reducing variability across repeated runs.
limitation: Uses only large proprietary closed-weight models, no quantization or LoRA fine-tuning on small open agents.

title: AgentWorld: Personality-Aware Reliability Evaluation for Agentic Information Retrieval
research_question: Can agentic IR reliability be evaluated under diverse simulated user personalities and perturbations?
models: not enumerated in abstract
core_finding: Combines pass^k consistency scoring with adversarial Monte-Carlo perturbation of required-state spines and reports pre-existing trajectory brittleness.
limitation: Framework demonstration on small case studies (5-10 tasks/personas).

title: AgentJudgeBench: A Multi-Difficulty Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Judges on Agentic Tool-Calling
research_question: How reliable are LLM judges when grading agentic tool-calling workflows?
models: generators 3B-70B open-weight plus GPT-5.4; judges 20B to frontier
core_finding: Judge alignment degrades monotonically with task difficulty and converges to a 77-82% band on hard queries without ground truth regardless of judge scale.
limitation: About grader reliability, not agent run-to-run consistency; matters because it bounds any LLM-judged consistency metric.

title: EDGE: Engine for Deterministic Graph Evaluation through Conversation Simulation from Graph Structured DSL Configuration
research_question: Does graph-structured agent configuration improve behavioral/trajectory determinism vs unconstrained agents?
models: Not specified; framework-agnostic (AgentGraph, LangGraph); no small open-weight model size given
benchmarks: Custom graph-traversal conversational trajectories via AgentGraph DSL
core_finding: Agents configured with explicit structured node transitions (AgentGraph/LangGraph) show superior determinism than unconstrained agents.
limitation: Focuses on graph-structure vs unconstrained comparison, not on quantization/LoRA effects or specific small open-weight model identities.

title: Testing Interchangeability in LLM Agent Teams
research_question: Are role-matched agents in a multi-agent team interchangeable?
models: several base models (ablated)
repeated_runs: yes, 8 teams x 10 formation episodes per setting
core_finding: Swapping role-matched agents costs little task score but raises communication per unit progress by 16-63% against a placebo control, and the penalty tracks decoding temperature and formation length.
limitation: Multi-agent teaming, not single-agent run-to-run consistency.

title: Chronicle: Cut-Point Replay for Regression Testing of LLM Agents
research_question: Can non-deterministic agent runs be recorded and replayed as regression tests?
models: simulated model boundaries
core_finding: Cut-point replay records an agent run at its non-deterministic boundaries and reproduces it bit-stably across 20 repetitions with zero model calls, converting a recorded incident into a CI regression test.
limitation: Engineering tool on 6 synthetic failures; no model-level variance measurement.

title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving
research_question: Does prefix caching cause run-to-run trajectory divergence in agentic LLM serving, and does quantization amplify it?
models: Not named in abstract; unclear if open-weight ≤7B used
benchmarks: 80-episode multi-turn agentic tool-use workload; single-turn bridge task
core_finding: Prefix caching causes trajectory divergence that rises sharply with quantization (36.2% at 16-bit vs 75.0% at 4-bit), while non-cached runs are bit-identical.
limitation: Focuses on caching as nondeterminism source rather than LoRA fine-tuning or inherent sampling variance, and model identities/sizes are not specified in the abstract.

title: Beyond Fluent Generation: A CPU Reliability Benchmark for MCP-Style Tool Calling in Sub-2B Small Language Models for Edge Deployment
research_question: How reliably can sub-2B open models emit valid MCP-style tool calls on CPU?
models: Phi-1.5, Pythia-1.4B, TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B (all open, <2B)
repeated_runs: yes, greedy vs nucleus sampling compared
core_finding: Under a recovery parser scoring parseability, tool-name correctness and argument completeness, Qwen2.5-1.5B reaches 75% greedy / 79% sampling and Qwen2.5-0.5B 72%.
limitation: Single-step tool emission, 100 prompts, no repeated-run consistency metric and no precision comparison.

title: Does RL Expand the Capability Boundary of LLM Agents? A PASS@(k,T) Analysis
research_question: Does RL expand the capability boundary of tool-using agents, or only improve reliability?
models: not fully named in abstract
repeated_runs: yes, pass-curves over sampling budget k
core_finding: Introduces PASS@(k,T); tool-use RL genuinely widens the pass-curve gap at large k, whereas supervised fine-tuning on matched data regresses the capability boundary on the same compositional tasks.
limitation: Trains with RL/SFT but does not report run-to-run behavioral consistency; relevant as a warning that SFT can narrow behavior.

title: Can Compressed LLMs Truly Act? An Empirical Evaluation of Agentic Capabilities in LLM Compression
research_question: How does post-training compression (quantization/pruning) affect LLM agentic capabilities across workflow, tool use, long-context, applications?
models: Gemma-2B, Qwen2.5 7B-32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill; includes open-weight model ≤7B (Gemma-2B)
benchmarks: ACBench: WorfBench, Needle-in-Haystack, tool use/function call tasks
core_finding: 4-bit quantization preserves workflow/tool-use but degrades real-world application accuracy by 10-15%.
limitation: Focuses on capability degradation under compression, not run-to-run consistency/variance of repeated agent executions on same input.

title: Dynamic Mixed-Precision Routing for Efficient Multi-step LLM Interaction
research_question: Can dynamic per-step precision routing cut inference cost while preserving multi-step decision-making accuracy?
models: Unspecified-size LLMs, quantized high/low precision; no explicit ≤7B open-weight model confirmed
core_finding: Dynamic mixed-precision routing across interaction steps achieves better accuracy-cost trade-off than single-precision baselines.
limitation: Focuses on cost-accuracy trade-off via routing, not on measuring run-to-run consistency/variance under fixed precision or LoRA fine-tuning.

title: Quantization Inflates Reasoning: Token Inflation as a Hidden Cost of Low-Bit Reasoning Models
research_question: Does low-bit quantization change reasoning behavior/length of LLM reasoning models, not just accuracy?
models: Unspecified reasoning LLMs with INT4/INT3 quantization; sizes/open-weight status not given
benchmarks: Math reasoning, code generation, science QA, agentic tool-use
core_finding: INT4/INT3 quantization preserves accuracy but inflates chain-of-thought length, offsetting per-token speedups.
limitation: Focuses on token-length/behavioral inflation under quantization but does not analyze run-to-run output consistency/variance on identical inputs.

title: Flat Score, Amplified Failures: How the Error Budget Masks Damage in Quantized LLM Agents
research_question: Does 4-bit/8-bit quantization degrade tool-calling agent process behavior despite flat task-success scores?
models: Two open-weight model families (dense and MoE variants); specific sizes/names not in abstract
benchmarks: τ²-bench, telecom and retail domains, 456 episodes/cell
core_finding: Quantization amplifies pre-existing failure modes (tool-name hallucination) in volume without changing task-success score, masked by the benchmark's error budget.
limitation: Focuses on quantization's effect on error volume/type rather than run-to-run variance on identical inputs, so consistency across repeated runs is not directly measured.

title: What Breaks Under Pruning in Smart Homes, and When? Evaluating LLM Degradation Across Architectures and Task Complexity
research_question: What capability breaks first when an LLM is pruned, in context-grounded tool calling?
models: 4 LLMs spanning dense Transformer, dense hybrid and MoE
core_finding: Dense models have narrow safe pruning regions followed by sharp degradation while MoE models tolerate much more pruning; pruning degrades grounded specificity (device, argument, value) before schema-level intent and aggressive dense pruning induces systematic over-refusal.
limitation: Pruning rather than quantization, single-turn tool calls, and degradation is measured on accuracy components rather than run-to-run consistency.

title: Quantization Thresholds Replicate, Failure Modes Do Not: A Three-Model Study of Agentic Tool Use in Polish from 8-bit to 2-bit
research_question: Does GGUF quantization precision affect agentic tool-use capability/failure modes across models?
models: Bielik-11B-v3.0, Bielik-Minitron-7B-v3.0, Llama-PLLuM-8B; all open-weight ≤11B (7B and 8B included)
core_finding: Agentic tool-use capability collapses sharply between 3-bit and 2-bit quantization across all three models, but the specific failure modes differ by model.
limitation: Focuses on quantization effects on single-run agentic accuracy rather than run-to-run consistency/variance on identical inputs, so direct repeatability metrics (pass^k) are not reported.

title: Quantization Meets Reasoning: Exploring and Mitigating Degradation of Low-Bit LLMs in Mathematical Reasoning
research_question: Where does PTQ degrade math reasoning stepwise, and how to mitigate while staying low-bit?
models: Qwen, LLaMA families 0.5-7B; includes open-weight models <=7B
core_finding: PTQ disproportionately causes early-step method/execution errors that cascade, and small targeted SFT/preference tuning recovers accuracy.
limitation: Focuses on math reasoning accuracy/degradation, not repeated-run consistency/variance or multi-step tool-use agent behavior.

title: Compressed Causal Reasoning: Quantization and GraphRAG Effects on Interventional and Counterfactual Accuracy
research_question: How does quantization (INT8/NF4) affect LLM accuracy on causal reasoning (association/intervention/counterfactual) tasks?
models: Llama 3 8B (open-weight, ≤7B boundary close, 8B); quantized INT8/NF4 variants
core_finding: Causal reasoning is broadly robust to quantization, with rung-2 interventional queries most sensitive and GraphRAG partially offsetting NF4 degradation.
limitation: Measures single-run accuracy per precision level, not variance/consistency across repeated runs on same input, and no agentic tool-use loop or LoRA trajectory distillation.

title: Three Roles, One Model: Role Orchestration at Inference Time to Close the Performance Gap Between Small and Large Agents
research_question: Can inference-time scaffolding close performance gap between small and large LLM agents under quantization?
models: Qwen3-8B (open-weight, FP16 & AWQ 4-bit); compared to DeepSeek-Coder 33B
core_finding: Three-tier inference scaffolding roughly doubles task completion for Qwen3-8B in both FP16 and AWQ settings, matching larger models.
limitation: Focuses on mean task success/capability under quantization rather than run-to-run variance or consistency on identical inputs.

title: Extreme Low-Bit Inference in Reasoning Models: Failure Modes and Targeted Recovery
research_question: How does 2-bit quantization cause reasoning-process failures in LRMs and can lightweight fixes recover accuracy?
models: Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B (open-weight; 8B qualifies as small open model)
core_finding: 2-bit quantization causes process-level failures (loops, budget exhaustion) degrading accuracy, which targeted FP16 planning/loop-rescue controls largely recover.
limitation: Focuses on single-run accuracy/trace pathology at one precision level rather than cross-run consistency or variance across repeated identical queries.

title: RATIO: Reasoning Analysis and Token-level Inference Optimization for Quantized Reasoning Models
research_question: How does PTQ affect reasoning model overthinking/length and accuracy, and how to mitigate?
models: Unspecified reasoning LLMs (full-precision vs quantized); no explicit ≤7B open-weight model named
benchmarks: Reasoning benchmarks (CoT accuracy/length); exact names unspecified
core_finding: RATIO identifies quantization-induced overthinking tokens and applies token-specific penalties, improving accuracy up to 9.8 points and cutting CoT length up to 51.3%.
limitation: Focuses on single-turn CoT reasoning length/accuracy, not on agentic tool-use or run-to-run consistency/variance under repeated sampling.

title: Structured Agent Distillation for Large Language Model
research_question: Does segment-aware distillation of teacher agent trajectories preserve reasoning/action fidelity in smaller student agents?
models: Large LLM teacher distilled into smaller student; sizes/names unspecified in abstract
core_finding: Structured, span-level distillation of reasoning and action segments outperforms token-level and imitation learning baselines with minimal performance drop under compression.
limitation: No evidence of measuring run-to-run consistency/variance across repeated identical inputs, nor any quantization analysis.

title: Distilling LLM Agent into Small Models with Retrieval and Code Tools
research_question: Can agent task-solving behavior (not just reasoning) be distilled from LLM agents into small models?
models: Teacher LLM agents distilled into sLMs 0.5B/1.5B/3B (open-weight, ≤7B used)
benchmarks: Eight reasoning tasks: factual QA and math, in/out-of-domain
core_finding: Agent distillation with first-thought prefix and self-consistent action generation lets small models match larger CoT-distilled models on tool-using tasks.
limitation: Focuses on distillation performance/generalization, not on repeated-run consistency or quantization effects for the same fixed input.

title: MapCoder-Lite: Distilling Multi-Agent Coding into a Single Small LLM
research_question: Can distillation and agent-wise LoRA fine-tuning compress multi-agent coding LLMs into one small 7B model?
models: 7B open-source model fine-tuned; distilled from large (>30B) LLM agents
core_finding: Agent-wise LoRA fine-tuning on distilled multi-agent trajectories lets a 7B model match much of a 32B multi-agent system's coding performance.
limitation: Focuses on coding accuracy/efficiency gains rather than run-to-run output consistency or variance across repeated executions.

title: R2V Agent: Teaching SLMs When to Ask for Help
research_question: When should a distilled small agent escalate a step to a stronger teacher model?
models: a distilled SLM student plus a stronger teacher LLM (sizes not in abstract)
benchmarks: interactive agent tasks (not named in abstract)
core_finding: Trains the student by behavioral cloning on teacher trajectories followed by verifier-guided DPO with consistency regularization, then escalates to the teacher only at steps where a calibrated router predicts residual failure risk.
limitation: Consistency enters as a training regularizer, not as a measured outcome; no quantization axis.

title: Agent-FLAN: Designing Data and Methods of Effective Agent Tuning for Large Language Models
research_question: How to design training data/methods to effectively fine-tune LLMs for agent tasks?
models: Llama2-7B/13B fine-tuned (open-weight, 7B qualifies as small)
benchmarks: Agent evaluation datasets (e.g. HotpotQA, ToolBench-like); custom hallucination benchmark
core_finding: Agent-FLAN's redesigned training corpus improves Llama2-7B agent performance by 3.5% and reduces hallucination.
limitation: Fine-tunes on curated agent corpus rather than explicit stronger-model agent trajectories, and does not assess run-to-run consistency.

title: DARA: Decomposition-Alignment-Reasoning Autonomous Language Agent for Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs
research_question: Can fine-tuning small LLMs on decomposition-alignment-reasoning trajectories improve KGQA agent performance?
models: Llama-2-7B, Mistral fine-tuned; compared vs GPT-4 ICL agent; open-weight ≤7B used
core_finding: DARA fine-tuned on small number of high-quality trajectories on Llama-2-7B/Mistral outperforms GPT-4 ICL agents and other fine-tuned agents in zero-shot KGQA.
limitation: No repeated-run variance/consistency analysis and no quantization study, only single-pass accuracy evaluation.

title: Internalizing Agency from Reflective Experience
pub_status: see arXiv comment: 17 pages, 5 figures; Submitted to ICML 2026
research_question: Can agents internalize recovery behavior by distilling their own reflective corrections?
models: not enumerated in abstract
core_finding: Outcome-driven post-training causes distribution sharpening that narrows behavior to already-successful trajectories, which LEAFE counters by distilling experience-guided corrections back into the policy.
limitation: Distribution sharpening is argued via pass@k, not measured as same-input behavioral variance.

title: Search, Do not Guess: Teaching Small Language Models to Be Effective Search Agents
research_question: Can fine-tuning improve small LM search-agent reliability vs. distillation from large LLMs?
models: Small LMs (e.g. Qwen-series SLMs, unspecified sizes) distilled from larger LLMs; likely open-weight ≤7B
core_finding: Proposed fine-tuning method trains SLMs to reliably search and ground answers, outperforming LLM-distillation baselines.
limitation: No explicit repeated-run variance/consistency analysis on identical inputs, and no quantization study.

title: Revisiting DAgger in the Era of LLM-Agents
research_question: Does DAgger-style training on teacher trajectories improve small LM agents on long-horizon SWE tasks?
models: 4B and 8B student models (open-weight, ≤7B boundary: 4B qualifies), teacher unspecified
core_finding: DAgger-style training on teacher trajectories outperforms SFT/RL baselines for 4B/8B SWE agents.
limitation: No repeated-run consistency analysis or quantization study; focuses on single-pass performance gains rather than behavioral variance across runs.

title: Compiling Agentic Workflows into LLM Weights: Near-Frontier Quality at Two Orders of Magnitude Less Cost
research_question: Can compiling multi-step agentic workflows into fine-tuned small-model weights match frontier orchestration quality cheaply?
models: Small fine-tuned models vs frontier model baseline; specific open-weight size/name not stated in abstract
benchmarks: Travel booking, Zoom support, insurance claims agent workflows
core_finding: Fine-tuning small models on workflow procedures ('subterranean agents') achieves near-frontier quality at much lower cost than orchestration.
limitation: No repeated-run consistency/variance analysis or quantization study is mentioned, so overlap with project's core reliability question is unclear.

title: DuoMem: Towards Capable On-Device Memory Agents via Dual-Space Distillation
research_question: Can LoRA/context distillation from a 72B teacher's trajectories make a 4B agent match teacher performance on ALFWorld?
models: 4B student, 72B teacher, ablations 2B-72B; open-weight models used but exact names/sizes unclear from abstract
core_finding: DuoMem's dual-space distillation boosts a 4B model from 4.3% to 77.9% task success, close to a 72B teacher's 87.1%.
limitation: Focuses on capability transfer via LoRA on agent trajectories but does not report run-to-run variance/consistency of the student agent on repeated identical inputs.

title: A Systematic Evaluation of Trajectory Data Curation for LoRA Fine-Tuning of Code Agents
research_question: How does trajectory quality/quantity filtering affect LoRA fine-tuning of code agents on expert trajectories?
models: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (open-weight, 7B, qualifies as small); trajectories from unspecified stronger model
benchmarks: SWE-trajectory dataset, SWE-bench resolve rate, CE loss, ROUGE-L
core_finding: Trajectory-level quality scoring (esp. error-retry rate) is a viable but scale-sensitive lever for LoRA SFT of code agents, validated via CE-loss/ROUGE-L proxy.
limitation: No repeated-run consistency/variance analysis on identical inputs and no quantization study, so only addresses T3 of the project's three questions.

title: Behavior Quotient Learning for Low-Rank Adaptation of LLM Agents
research_question: Can a single LoRA adapter efficiently learn diverse agent behaviors from heterogeneous trajectories without rank/routing overhead?
models: Not specified in abstract; base LLM agent fine-tuned via LoRA, no model size/open-weight info given
core_finding: BQ-LoRA improves single-adapter LoRA fine-tuning on diverse agent trajectories by balancing redundant updates and preserving decision distributions under rank constraints.
limitation: No evidence of measuring run-to-run consistency/variance or quantization effects; relevance limited to the LoRA-on-agent-trajectories fine-tuning aspect only.

title: Coaching Qwen3 Coder 30B to Think Like a CodeClash Arena Agent
research_question: Can fine-tuning on stronger-agent trajectories improve a weak open-weight coding agent's arena performance?
models: Qwen3-Coder-30B (open-weight, >7B) fine-tuned; teacher is stronger commercial agents incl. Qwen3 Coder Plus
core_finding: ReAct SFT and trajectory-quality weighted SFT improve strategic behavior so fine-tuned Qwen3-Coder-30B beats Qwen3 Coder Plus in tournaments.
limitation: Model studied (30B) is larger than the ≤7B scale of interest and paper does not analyze run-to-run consistency or quantization.

title: Don't Mask the Environment: Observation Supervision Changes How Agents Explore Under RL
research_question: Should supervised fine-tuning on agent trajectories also supervise environment-observation tokens?
models: Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B (open, in the project's range)
core_finding: Supervising observation tokens during trajectory SFT performs the same as action-only SFT after SFT but yields higher pass@k after GRPO, trading some pass@1 reliability for breadth at 8B.
limitation: pass@k is used as a coverage metric, not as a same-input consistency metric; no quantization axis.

title: The Fellowship of the Query: Learning Retrieval Actions
research_question: Can LoRA fine-tuning on teacher trajectories improve small LMs as retrieval-agent next-action controllers?
models: Granite 4.1 3B (open-weight, ≤7B); TF-IDF logistic-regression baseline; other SLMs/xSLMs controllers
benchmarks: HotpotQA-style QA trajectories (1,646 held-out actions, 149 trajectories)
core_finding: LoRA fine-tuning on teacher action trajectories substantially improves small-model next-action prediction and end-to-end QA metrics over zero-shot prompting.
limitation: No analysis of run-to-run variance/consistency on repeated identical inputs, and no quantization comparison.

title: Graph-Conditioned On-Policy Agent Distillation from Off-the-Shelf Teachers
research_question: Can graph-conditioned on-policy distillation from off-the-shelf teachers improve small agent success rates?
models: 4B student agent; teachers off-the-shelf/GRPO-trained (sizes unspecified); 4B is ≤7B open-weight
core_finding: GC-OPD substantially improves mean success over vanilla OPD and other baselines on ScienceWorld, ALFWorld, and WebShop using small student agents.
limitation: Focuses on mean success improvement via distillation, not on run-to-run variance/consistency of the resulting agent across repeated identical inputs.
